title: Building this site from scratch
summary: Kicking off the project — planning the design system and building the HTML/CSS foundation before any JavaScript.
content: Before writing any JavaScript, I spent time on the HTML and CSS foundation: a shared stylesheet with design tokens (colors, fonts, spacing), then six pages built on top of it — Home, About, Resume, Projects, Blog, and Contact. Getting the structure and styling consistent first made every JavaScript feature afterward much easier to slot in, since the markup and class names were already predictable across pages.

title: Adding a dark mode toggle with localStorage
summary: How I built the light/dark theme switcher and made the preference persist across pages using localStorage.
content: The theme switcher works by toggling a data-theme attribute on the body element, with CSS custom properties defined for both light and dark values. The trickier part was making the preference persist: every time the theme changes, it's saved with localStorage.setItem('theme', theme), and on every page load, a small inline script reads it back with localStorage.getItem('theme') before the page even fully renders — this prevents a visible flash of the wrong theme while the rest of the JavaScript loads. One challenge was that the toggle button eventually got moved into a dynamically-loaded header component, which meant the theme setup code needed to be re-run after the header finished loading, not just once on page load.
